house-rules.title: House Rules
house-rules.content:
The rules we play by

D&D 5e, 2014 rules. We don’t use the 2024 rules: no weapon mastery, no origin feats at 1st level, no Heroic Inspiration (regular inspiration works as in the 2014 Player’s Handbook).
D&D Beyond sometimes mixes 2024 material into a 2014 character. If your sheet shows weapon mastery properties or 2024 actions, ignore them.
Levels: you start at 1st level. We use milestone levelling: you level up at important moments in the story, not by counting experience points.

Building a character

Ability scores: point buy (27 points).
Hit points: maximum at 1st level. Each level after that, gain the fixed average for your class (d6: 4, d8: 5, d10: 6, d12: 7) plus your Constitution modifier. On D&D Beyond, set Hit Point Type to Fixed.
Starting equipment or gold: either option from the Player’s Handbook is fine.
Your purse: whatever coin your character starts with is what they bring to the carnival, and they pay their own way. Expect a ticket to cost a few silver pieces, games and treats a handful of coppers, and the odd extra a silver piece or so. Nobody needs to spend a fortune, but keep some coin to hand.
Books we use: the Player’s Handbook, Dungeon Master’s Guide and Monster Manual (2014), and The Wild Beyond the Witchlight.
From The Wild Beyond the Witchlight: the fairy and harengon races, and the Feylost and Witchlight Hand backgrounds. You’ll find them on D&D Beyond.

Fairy: at our table, fairies also have Soft Landing: you have resistance to falling damage.


Custom backgrounds are fine, following the rules in the Player’s Handbook: two skills, two tool or language proficiencies, and matching starting equipment. Talk to the DM.
Other books and homebrew: options from other books, or homebrew, may be possible. Ask the DM.

At the table

Talk to the DM about anything you’d rather not see in the game, or would like to see more of.
Your character’s secrets stay between you and the DM. What other players learn about your character, they learn in play.

the-carnival-flyer.title: The Carnival Flyer
the-carnival-flyer.content:
These turned up overnight, pinned to every door, fence post and tavern board for miles around. Nobody saw who put them there.



                  
                  Mister Witch & Mister Light present 
                  
                

The Witchlight Carnival
Returned at last, after eight long years!
Wonders from a hundred kingdoms and a hundred worlds, gathered in a single field.
Thrill to the acrobats of the Big Top! Ride the Carousel that never stops! Lose yourself in the Hall of Illusions, glide across the lake on the Gondola Swans, and cheer on the fastest snails you’ll ever see!
Feast in the Feasting Orchard, try your luck at a hundred games of skill, and carry home prizes you won’t find anywhere else.
And in the last hour before dawn, one lucky guest will be crowned the Witchlight Monarch!
Gates open at dusk. Gates close before dawn.
Admission: grown folk, 8 silver. Little ones, 3 silver.
Short of coin? Our ticketer loves a fair trade.


On the back of every ticket


                  
                  Three little rules keep the Witchlight bright 
                  
                


Every gift is owed a gift.
Be a good guest, and we’ll be a good host.
What isn’t yours stays where it is.




Mister Witch and Mister Light, the carnival’s owners, as they appear on the posters.
Small print, very small indeed: the management accepts no responsibility for lost property, lost time or lost hearts.

what-people-say.title: What People Say

index.title: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight
index.content:
A fairy tale with teeth.
Once every eight years, a carnival comes to town. Nobody sees it arrive. One evening there are empty fields at the edge of the woods, and the next there are tents striped in every color, lanterns strung between the trees, and music drifting out of a calliope that never seems to need anyone to play it. Its gates open at dusk and close before dawn, and after a few nights it’s gone again.
They call it the Witchlight Carnival. People say it has travelled everywhere: to every kingdom, every world, places no map has heard of. People say you can find anything there, if you know where to look. People say a lot of things.
This campaign begins on the night the carnival returns.
What to expect

Whimsy on top, loss and bargains underneath. Talking animals, snail races and sugar cupcakes, and under all of it, old promises, stolen things and people who don’t play fair.
Cleverness counts. Many problems can be solved by talking, trading, tricking or understanding them. Fighting is always an option; it isn’t always the best one.
You arrive separately. Each of your characters comes to the carnival for their own reasons, and none of you know each other yet. How you meet is part of the story.
Your stories matter. Each of your characters’ pasts is woven into what happens.
We play D&D 5e (2014 rules). See House Rules.

On this site

The Carnival Flyer: the flyer that’s been nailed up all over town.
What People Say: rumours and tall tales about the carnival.
